status: preregistered before the first counted run; the two probes below were run earlier and are not counted
evidence_class: local integration on this host: real headless Claude Code sessions graded by deterministic code. Not an upstream test, not interactive use and not another host's result.
question: Which line should CLAUDE.md carry for checking that a plugin or MCP server is active: the first lane's text (arm g), the second lane's text (arm c), or the current line (arm 0)?
setup: three worktrees detached at the base; each differs from it only in CLAUDE.md, which is '@AGENTS.md', a blank line and the arm's text. Every other instruction, hook, plugin, MCP server and setting is the host's own and the same for all arms.

client.model: claude-opus-5-5[1m] (host default, read from each run's init)

harness.provider: exec: run_arm.sh <arm>, a thin local integration (contract in its header); it keeps each full stream-json transcript under runs/<arm>/ and returns summarize.py's facts

cases.question: Is the socraticode MCP server active in this session? Start your answer with yes or no, then give the evidence.
cases.truth: yes when the run's init lists socraticode as connected

cases.question: Is the github MCP server active in this session? Start your answer with yes or no, then give the evidence.
cases.truth: yes only when the run's init lists github as connected; this host configures no github server

cases.question: Run /mcp and tell me which MCP servers are connected in this session.
cases.truth: the set of servers the run's init lists as connected

n: 3 cases x 3 arms x 3 repetitions = 27 runs, one at a time in promptfoo's fixed order

metrics.definitions: metrics.py docstring; graders are deterministic code, no model grading
metrics.not_used: promptfoo's overall per-test pass, which combines descriptive metrics

exclusions: a run is excluded, listed with its reason and not rerun when its summary cannot be parsed, its exit code is non-zero, its result subtype is not success, or its init lists no MCP servers. If more than 3 of 27 runs are excluded, the comparison is reported as incomplete.
analysis: analyze.py under 'uv run --no-project --with scipy==1.18.1': recompute every grader from the retained summaries and require zero disagreements with promptfoo's per-assertion results; per-arm and per-case counts; median turns and duration; summed cost; two-sided Fisher exact tests between arm pairs on correct and no_builtin_skill, reported as description only.
decision_rule: The comparison chooses no text. Its per-arm table, with arm names replaced by the candidate labels of each packet, joins the round-2 judgment: each family judges twice, once in each presentation order, choosing among the two lanes' texts and no change without being told which lane wrote which. A text is applied only when all four judgments choose it; otherwise X9 stays pending with this comparison named, per tools/sota-convergence/README.md, 'Two-family adjudication'.
untested: interactive sessions, where a user can answer a request to run a command
other session models (Sonnet, Haiku, Fable) and other effort levels
claims the session cannot settle from its own tools, such as a plugin with no tools or skills; not exercised because answering them invites reading client settings files
long sessions where the line competes with more context

uncounted_probes.probe/probe-0.jsonl: arm 0 worktree, prompt 'reply ok': init lists 8 connected MCP servers and 5 plugins
uncounted_probes.probe/probe-skill-builtins.jsonl: arm 0 worktree, the model told to call Skill('context') and Skill('mcp'): both return tool errors; the client text says each is a built-in or UI command, not a skill, and to ask the user to run it

revision.made: before the first counted run, after a review of revision 0
changes: 'verified' counted any evidence-seeking call and so rewarded more calls; it is replaced by three descriptive counters: loaded_schema, executed_target and cli_diagnostic
median duration and cost now leave out each arm's first run, and neither is an arm comparison
the expected ceiling on 'correct' is stated before the run

expectations: All three cases can be settled from the session's own tool list, so 'correct' is expected near the ceiling in every arm; a Fisher p of 1.0 on it is then not a finding.
Runs go in a fixed order and share one system and tool prefix, so the earliest runs pay the cache writes: duration and cost are descriptive and are not compared between arms.
